title: Admission Orchestrator and Attention Coalescer to reduce tail latency in continuous batching
creator: Maya Lopez
description:
Summary:
We will build an 'Admission Orchestrator' that combines request-level admission control with a lightweight 'Attention Coalescer' layer to improve kernel selection and reduce 95/99 token latency in continuous batching workloads. Goal is to reduce tail latency spikes caused by heterogeneous request sizes, attention pattern variance, and suboptimal kernel switching while keeping or improving aggregate throughput and token cost.

Why now:
- Production traces show intermittent 99th token latency spikes (up to 3.5x baseline) under mixed short/long workloads.
- Existing queue-based admission reduces some tails but frequently triggers kernel thrash when batch composition swings.
- Kernel-selection heuristics are coarse-grained; we can leverage lightweight attention-profile hints to avoid expensive kernel warmups.

Design overview:
1) Admission Orchestrator: a modular controller placed at the request ingress that maintains short-lived micro-queues by affinity. It admits requests into micro-batches using three signals: priority SLA, estimated token cost, and attention-profile fingerprint. Admission decisions support preemption windows and a small 'grace buffer' to allow coalescing without incurring decode stalls.
2) Attention Coalescer: a sampler that computes a compact attention-profile hash (e.g., dense vs sparse-like patterns, average window length) during prefill or first-token evaluation. The coalescer provides kernel-affinity hints to the runtime kernel selector to prefer kernels that minimize warm-up overhead when serving the upcoming decode token stream.
3) Kernel-affinity API: a short RPC/metadata field added to requests that expresses desired kernel variants (e.g., nvfuser-optimized, int8-quantized fallback, attention-optimized). Kernel selection continues to fall back if the requested kernel is not available, but the orchestrator prefers queues with available affinity.

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Spike (Week 1): implement attention-profile sampler and offline analyzer; run on production trace to classify common patterns. (owner: Ari)
- Prototype (Week 2): add admission orchestrator with two micro-queue classes (latency-sensitive, batch-friendly) and kernel-affinity metadata; simulate on staging traffic replay. (owner: Maya/Ari)
- Integration (Week 3): wire kernel-affinity hints into runtime kernel selector; add telemetry for queue composition and kernel-switch counts. (owner: Runtime team lead)
- Canary (Week 4): rollout via feature flag to 5% traffic with strict SLO guardrails and automated rollback on regression. (owner: SRE + Runtime)
- Post-canary (Week 5): expand to 50% and tune admission thresholds.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- 95th token latency reduced by >= 25% on mixed short/long workloads in canary region.
- 99th token latency reduced by >= 30% or absolute 99th < 2x median.
- No more than 5% regression in overall tokens/sec throughput.
- Kernel-switch events per minute reduced by >= 40% on measured workloads.

Rollout and safeguards:
- Feature flag + per-route SLO checks. If SLO breach detected, orchestrator will auto-disable for that route and emit a rollback incident.
- Conservative defaults: micro-queue wait windows small (<= 8ms) to avoid user-visible delay.
- Metric-backed kill switch: if any of the success metrics hit a negative threshold (latency regressions, error rate increase), automatic rollback.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Risk: attention-profile sampling adds CPU overhead at ingress; we must keep the sampler sub-microsecond per request. We'll evaluate a sampled-path approach (e.g., sample 10% of requests for detailed profiling).
- Complexity: kernel-affinity introduces routing complexity and resource fragmentation; mitigation via soft-affinity (preference, not strict placement) and dynamic defragmentation jobs.
- Observability: need low-latency metrics for micro-queue fill rates and kernel warmup timings. We'll add new tracing spans and aggregate dashboards.

updates: 2026-03-10 - Triage: identified need after incident INC-2026-0214 where 99th token latency spiked during peak. Scoped as P0 given customer-visible latency.
2026-03-11 - Architecture sketch completed; attention-profile fingerprint defined (3-byte fingerprint + variance score). Submitted design doc for review.
2026-03-12 - Spike results: attention-profile classification reduced kernel-choice entropy by ~35% on sample traces. Observed ~6% CPU overhead with naive sampler; moving to sampled path to reduce.
2026-03-13 - Prototype PR created (draft). Implemented micro-queue logic with two classes and simple grace windows. Staging replay shows 20% 95th reduction in some scenarios; more tuning needed.
2026-03-14 - Blocker: need kernel-selector change to accept affinity hints; coordinating with kernel team. Also adding telemetry events for kernel-switch counters.
